public.title: Middleware Pipeline
public.description: Execute stages left to right. Each is {op,value}, op add, multiply, or stop. add/multiply transforms the integer accumulator; stop returns its value immediately, ignoring later stages. Return final integer; all intermediate values are guaranteed within 1000000. Stages model middleware continuation without executable functions. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: A stop stage terminates the pipeline before later transformations.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Transform one accumulator in stage order; stop returns immediately. O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
